references.text: An eternal prohibition against eating blood and fat, applying to all generations and all places where the Israelites live.
A detailed prohibition against eating blood, with an explanation that the blood contains life, and a repetition of the penalty of being cut off from the people.
The first prohibition against eating blood, given to Noah after the flood, as the basis for this commandment.
Moses repeats the prohibition against eating blood and commands that the blood be poured out on the ground like water.
Further command not to eat blood, because the blood is life, and a promise of blessing upon obedience.
Reminder not to eat blood in connection with rules concerning firstborn animals.
Saul rebukes the people for eating meat with blood, showing that the prohibition was practiced in Israel.
Ezekiel rebukes those who eat meat with blood as one of the sins leading to judgment.
The Jerusalem council requires Gentile Christians to abstain from blood, continuing this prohibition into the new covenant.
The letter from the apostolic council confirms the prohibition against eating blood as binding for Gentile Christians.
Paul is reminded of the decision from the apostolic council, including the prohibition against blood.
